name: Digitide Solutions Ltd
title: Digitide Solutions Ltd - 544413 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Digitide Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% QoQ to INR 760 crore, but EBITDA rose 2.5% to INR 79 crore (10.4% margin) and TCV nearly doubled to ~INR 400 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue was about INR 760 crore, down 2% sequentially, as management deliberately exited low-return work and repriced contracts. EBITDA rose 2.5% QoQ to about INR 79 crore, with margin up 45 bps to 10.4%, and reported PAT rose to INR 8.9 crore from INR 2.9 crore in Q1 with no exceptional items. Sales momentum improved: TCV rose 95% QoQ to nearly INR 400 crore and AI-led revenue doubled to INR 30.5 crore. Management reiterated a 200 bps full-year EBITDA margin improvement target but gave no numerical revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 2.9 crore in Q1 (tripled)
vs INR 12 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: India BPM
segments.commentary: Margin slightly declined to 13.6%; management cited wage revisions, repricing of existing contracts and exits of low-return work. India BPO is about 50-52% of wallet share.

segments.name: Tech & digital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 244 crore, +6.6% YoY; segment margin rose 315 bps to 11.1%. Platforms are expected to earn 2-3x BPO profitability per management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 323 crore, +13.5% YoY, 42.5% of revenue. International BPO is about 6-7% of wallet share.

segments.name: GCC / BOT
segments.commentary: Signed a BOT mandate to hire 1,000 people in the Philippines; about 700 already mobilised. Five GCC implementations in total, four managed-services.

segments.name: AI revenue
segments.commentary: INR 30.5 crore, split roughly 35-37% AI BPM, 30-35% platforms, 27-28% professional services; 4.1% of revenue vs 1.9% in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 target of 200 bps EBITDA margin improvement reiterated; management said it is a tough challenge and 45 bps QoQ was already delivered.
Management expects an exit-year EBITDA margin around 13%, which an analyst asked about; management said it remains committed but did not restate the figure explicitly.
Cost-structure actions are expected to be visible in H2 FY27; DSO expected to improve in H2.
TCV conversion rule of thumb: 30-35% of FY27 TCV expected to convert to revenue this fiscal; platforms take 10-16 weeks from booking to realisation, BPO 4-6 weeks.
No numerical revenue or EBITDA guidance beyond the margin target; management will update on AWS co-sell and EXM/insurance platform progress in Q3.
Alldigi buyback of about INR 48 crore; Digitide's stake is about 73.39%. Proceeds to go predominantly to reduce standalone debt.
capex_capacity: AI lab set up in Bangalore; AI centre of excellence in Coimbatore with 25+ hires.
Two delivery capability centres: Canada (insurance platform) and Chennai (EXM platform).
Philippines BOT mandate: 1,000 hires, about 700 already on board.
Six new live implementations on data, AI and cloud work during Q2.
demand_pricing: TCV ~INR 400 crore in Q2 vs INR 205 crore in Q1; mix shifted toward tech & digital and international.
AI deal share of ACV bookings rose to 29% (INR 160 crore ACV) from 14% (INR 118 crore) in Q1.
Sales funnel rose to INR 170 crore from INR 100 crore in Q1; AI funnel up about 70% QoQ.
Repricing and renegotiation volume up 2.5x QoQ; management is exiting contracts below return thresholds.
India BPM pivoting from T&M/headcount pricing to outcome-based models; AI pitched more in international BPO than India.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give numerical guidance on revenue and EBITDA, and is the 13% exit margin still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to quality of revenue, sales momentum and mix shift; it reiterated the 200 bps full-year target and said it remains committed, without restating the exit number.

qa_highlights.question: Alldigi buyback size and merger status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Alldigi board proposed a buyback of about INR 48 crore; Digitide holds 73.39% and will receive its share depending on other shareholders' participation. Merger is for the respective boards to decide.

qa_highlights.question: Why are PBT margins squeezed despite high EBITDA, given lease liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease costs hit PBT but not EBITDA; PBT rose to INR 14 crore from INR 12 crore YoY. Issues in India BPM (wage revisions, repricing, walk-aways) will take more than a quarter to fix.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on Alldigi's product rather than low-margin tech & digital services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platforms earn 2-3x BPO profitability and require an ARR/licence go-to-market; EXM business is about INR 150-160 crore, being taken to Middle East, Southeast Asia and SMB.

qa_highlights.question: How is TCV split between new logos and renewals, and how fast does it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a new-logo vs renewal split; it said 30-35% of FY27 TCV is expected to convert to revenue this fiscal, with platforms taking 10-16 weeks and BPO 4-6 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the AWS and Anthropic alliance economics?
qa_highlights.answer: AWS partnership is at advanced tier, value currently sub-INR 10 million with a target of 5x at premier tier; first buy-from deal done in US and payroll services sold to AWS in India.

risks_watch: Revenue decline (-2% QoQ) from deliberate exits; sustaining volumes while repricing.
India BPM margin dip to 13.6% and wage/repricing pressure; full-year 200 bps margin target needs H2 delivery.
DSO rose to ~84 days from 82; H2 collections improvement is a key test.
Net cash fell (analyst noted cash drain); no M&A deal yet despite repeated pipeline commentary.
Lease liabilities (H1 ~INR 85 crore) weigh on PBT versus EBITDA.
Q3 updates promised on AWS co-sell, EXM and insurance platform progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on directional progress (TCV, AI revenue, tech & digital margins) but cautious and non-committal on numerical targets, M&A timing and the India BPM turnaround, which management said will take more than a quarter.
key_quotes: Despite the sequential decline, our EBITDA increased to approximately INR 79 crores, up 2.5% Q-on-Q, and the EBITDA margin improved by 45 basis points to 10.4%.
We have continued to re-negotiate contracts and are not shying away to move from businesses that does not meet our return thresholds.
Our TCV booked in the quarter increased by 95% sequentially from INR 205 crores in Q1 to almost INR 400 crores in Q2.
H1 was about putting the foundations in place. H2 is all about converting those foundations into execution, profitable growth, and stronger cash generation.

adds.what: Philippines BOT mandate to hire 1,000 people (about 700 already mobilised)
AI centre of excellence in Coimbatore (25+ hires) and AI lab in Bangalore
Delivery capability centres in Canada (insurance platform) and Chennai (EXM platform)

growth.why: No numerical revenue guidance; only a reiterated ~200 bps FY27 EBITDA margin expansion target (not re-quantified), backed by cost actions in H2, repricing and TCV of ~INR 400 cr (30-35% expected to convert to FY27 revenue), while Q2 revenue fell 2% QoQ to ~INR 760 cr.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated ~200 bps FY27 EBITDA margin improvement target with 45 bps QoQ already delivered (Q2 margin 10.4%), and cost-structure actions are expected to show in H2 FY27, though management called it a tough challenge.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Delivery centres (Canada, Chennai), AI lab in Bangalore and Coimbatore CoE, and Philippines BOT of 1,000 hires (about 700 mobilised) are already in place, but these are minor adds with no capex figure disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: TCV nearly doubled to about INR 400 crore and the sales funnel rose to INR 170 crore from INR 100 crore, with 30-35% of FY27 TCV expected to convert, but revenue fell 2% QoQ and headcount is down 7% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed on the call and no capex figure or utilisation level was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical revenue or EBITDA guidance was given, and Q2 revenue fell 2% QoQ to about INR 760 crore as low-return work was exited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 200 bps full-year margin target needs H2 delivery while India BPM margin slipped to 13.6% and DSO rose to about 84 days from 82, and management said the BPM turnaround will take more than a quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AWS co-sell and EXM/insurance platform progress are due for update in Q3, and platforms are being taken to Middle East, Southeast Asia and SMB, with AI revenue up to INR 30.5 crore (4.1% of revenue).

rows.label: TCV conversion of FY27 bookings
rows.why: Management expects 30-35% of FY27 TCV (about INR 400 crore in Q2 alone, vs INR 205 crore in Q1) to convert to revenue this fiscal, with platforms taking 10-16 weeks and BPO 4-6 weeks.

rows.label: India BPM repricing and outcome-based pivot
rows.why: Repricing and renegotiation volume rose 2.5x QoQ and management is exiting below-threshold contracts, with cost actions expected visible in H2; BPM margin slipped to 13.6%.

rows.label: Alldigi buyback proceeds to reduce standalone debt
rows.why: Alldigi buyback of about INR 48 crore, with Digitide's 73.39% stake receiving its share depending on other shareholders' participation; net cash is about INR 76 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on TCV, AI revenue and tech & digital margins but non-committal on numerical targets, the 13% exit margin, M&A timing and the India BPM turnaround; analysts pushed on the exit margin, lease-driven PBT squeeze, cash drain and DSO.
